exposure: Maternal single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in human leukocyte antigen G (HLA-G) gene
cohort: 99 pregnant women (51 with severe PE and 48 with normal delivery)
finding: A specific SNP in the HLA-G gene (locus 29799440) was associated with preeclampsia susceptibility in Han Chinese pregnant women, with the CC genotype having a lower risk of PE compared to the TT genotype.
mod_finding: The study found an increased proportion of cesarean sections in the preeclampsia group compared to the normal delivery group.
birth_weight: Neonatal weight was significantly lower in the PE group (p < .001).
